name: Bluebeam Revu
subcategory: PDF markup and takeoff for AEC
tagline: PDF markup, measurement and takeoff software built around architecture and construction drawing sets.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The parts that look like the product, render a PDF, draw a cloud, add a callout, are genuinely a one-shot build on pdf.js plus pdf-lib. The parts that are actually the product are not: calibrated measurement you would stake a bid on, Studio Sessions where six people mark the same sheet live, sheet sets with auto-labeling and hyperlinks, document compare, OCR, batch stamping, and markup that a reviewer on the other end can open and reply to in their copy. It is also not a CAD tool, so the DIY framing of 'draw architectural diagrams' is aiming at the wrong thing anyway. A personal markup viewer is useful if you are the only person who ever sees the file. The moment a GC, an architect or a plan checker is on the other side of it, you are back to the thing everyone else already opens.
coreLoopDIY: A local web app that opens large PDFs, lets you draw scaled measurements plus standard markups on a layer, and exports a flattened annotated copy.
requirements: Local disk space for large drawing PDFs
Nothing else: no accounts, no cloud
whatYouLose: Studio Sessions: real time co-markup on the same sheet with an audit trail
Takeoff toolsets, quantity roll-ups and the Excel/CSV handoff estimators actually use
Round-trip markup fidelity: the other party can open, filter and reply to your markups in their Revu
Sheet set handling at scale: auto-labeling, page hyperlinks, compare documents, OCR, batch stamps
Defensible measurement: calibration, dimension precision and a stamped record people accept as-is
moatNotes: Every subcontractor, plan checker and PM in the chain already has it installed, which makes it the file format as much as the app.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because markup is a conversation, not a document. A construction set moves through a designer, a GC, a dozen subs and a jurisdiction, and each of them expects to receive markups they can filter, answer and stamp in the same tool. Paying per seat is cheaper than being the one person whose comments arrive as flattened pixels nobody can respond to, and far cheaper than a takeoff that was off because the scale was eyeballed. The license is not buying a PDF editor, it is buying membership in how the industry already exchanges redlines.
notes: The viewer and the markup layer are a long weekend, the measurement math is a week, the ecosystem is not for sale. The moat is that everyone downstream of you already opens Revu, so your redlines only count if they arrive in its language.
prompt:
Build a local, single-user PDF markup and measurement tool. No accounts, no cloud, no telemetry.

Stack, non-negotiable:
- Vite + React + TypeScript, single page app
- pdf.js for rendering, canvas overlay for annotations
- pdf-lib for export
- Dexie (IndexedDB) for storage
- Tailwind for UI
- Runs with `npm install && npm run dev`, no backend, no .env needed

Core loop:
1. Drag a PDF in. Store the file bytes in IndexedDB keyed by a hash so reopening is instant.
2. Render one page at a time with pan, zoom to fit, zoom to 400 percent, and a tile cache so 3000x2000 point drawing sheets stay smooth.
3. Markup tools on an overlay layer: freehand pen, rectangle, ellipse, revision cloud, arrow, text callout with leader, highlight. Each markup has color, line weight, opacity, author label and a created timestamp.
4. Measurement tools: a calibrate action where the user draws a known distance and types the real length plus unit, stored per page. Then linear distance, polyline length, rectangular and polygon area, and a count tool that drops numbered pins. Show live values while drawing and a running total per tool per page.
5. Left sidebar: page thumbnails. Right sidebar: markup list grouped by page, click to zoom to that markup, checkbox to show or hide, delete.
6. Export: a flattened annotated PDF via pdf-lib, and a CSV of every measurement and count with page, tool, label and value.
7. Undo and redo across all markup operations. Autosave to IndexedDB after every change.

Explicitly out of scope, do not attempt:
- Any multi-user, sync, sharing or comment reply features
- OCR, document compare, batch processing, form field editing
- CAD authoring or vector editing of the original page content
- Editing page text or images

Ship a README with the calibration workflow, a note that measurements are only as good as the calibration, and a warning that exported markups are flattened and not re-editable by other PDF tools.
